### NA-09 — Nonlinear equations and Newton methods

**Pages:** nonlinear-equations-and-newton-methods / nonlinear-equations-and-newton-methods-examples.

**Scope:** Define fixed-point iteration, damped Newton and a finite-difference Jacobian variant with explicit input/output and stopping status. Prove local quadratic convergence of ordinary variable-Jacobian Newton only for F∈C³, DF invertible in a neighborhood of a root, and a sufficiently close initial point. Reuse the local frozen-Jacobian contraction only for its stated map; it is not ordinary Newton. No arbitrary-start or global convergence theorem is claimed.

**Proof route:** Taylor-expand F(x_j) at the root, use a uniform local inverse-Jacobian bound and a local invariant ball to derive ||e_{j+1}||≤C||e_j||², then prove the iterate remains in that ball. For line search, prove only the stated accepted-step decrease under its assumptions; distinguish convergence of the nonlinear solve from discretization accuracy.

**Examples:** scalar Newton near a simple root; double root with reduced order; a starting point outside the local basin; frozen versus updated Jacobian.

**Requires:** published thm-banach-fixed-point, cor-banach-error-estimates, lem-newton-contraction-near-an-invertible-derivative, thm-multivariable-taylor-formula-with-lagrange-remainder, and the exact ODE IVP page when the nonlinear equation is a shooting residual.

**Sources:** Hairer–Wanner, Ch. VI §VI.3, PDF pp. 6–8 / printed pp. 139–141, read by the recovery reader: https://www.unige.ch/~hairer/poly/chap6.pdf; FNC Ch. 4 selected files rootproblem.md, newton.md, newtonsys.md read at commit a280ed1a013393ee0a184dcbaa866522f35a3516: https://github.com/fncbook/fnc/tree/a280ed1a013393ee0a184dcbaa866522f35a3516. ## XA-01 — extend canonical rare-event/SMC guarantees; do not duplicate algorithms

**Existing home:** `library/bayesian-computational-statistics/feynman-kac-particle-filters.md` and its examples. Existing `alg-sequential-importance-resampling`, `alg-multinomial-and-residual-offspring-resampling`, `thm-sequential-particle-estimator-is-unbiased`, `lem-feynman-kac-path-measures-satisfy-forward-recursion` retain their homes. Existing IS unbiasedness, finite variance and CLT are already covered; no new IS pair.

**New delta.** Integration owner: optimization/statistics RARE1 absorbs this amendment; no separate pair or competing procedure. Define a finite sequence of nested events/levels with exact stopped transition kernels and potentials 0≤G≤1. Prove measurability of finite-budget stopped kernels (or a declared exact-hitting oracle), connection of their Feynman–Kac normalizer to the target event probability, and error of any time-discretized crossing approximation separately. Use existing SMC product-normalizer estimator; its unbiasedness is reused only under all positive-prefix-normalizer/full-resampling hypotheses. Then prove a finite-horizon L2 bound with explicit dependence on number of levels, prefix probabilities, bounded normalized potentials and kernel mixing. A safe first contract is an O(1/N) **absolute** mean-square bound for a fixed number of bounded-potential levels, proved by conditional variance and induction. Relative error divides by the squared rare probability and may be huge. An efficiency claim uniform in rarity needs an additional theorem and actual lower bounds/minorization; not “splitting reduces variance” by name.

**Missing local suppliers / owner.** Local to this amendment: stopped-kernel construction and cemetery handling; Feynman–Kac event identity; conditional empirical variance identity for the actual resampling procedure; finite-level martingale/variance recursion; bias from approximate crossing/hitting kernels. Existing finite-horizon SMC unbiasedness does not by itself imply finite-particle accuracy or uniform-in-time stability (the canonical page explicitly says so). No adaptive-level unbiasedness without its separate order-statistic/martingale proof. Root must assign this amendment to the statistics guarantee owner and check affected consumers if an existing statement changes; prefer new theorem carriers without altering original definitions.

**Examples.** Reliability chain crossing; extinction estimate; all particles die (zero estimate, not algorithmic proof of zero probability); an IS proposal with infinite weighted second moment; same budget splitting with worse relative error. **Sources:** Cérou–Del Moral–Furon–Guyader, “Sequential Monte Carlo for rare event estimation,” Statistics and Computing 22 (2012), pp. 795–808, DOI `10.1007/s11222-011-9231-6`; Del Moral, *Feynman–Kac Formulae* (2004), particle variance/martingale chapters, DOI `10.1007/978-1-4684-9393-1`. ### NA-43 — Numerical optimization for statistical computation

**Pages:** numerical-optimization-for-statistical-computation / numerical-optimization-for-statistical-computation-examples.

**Scope:** For C² f on an open convex domain, an attained interior minimum and initial sublevel set compactly contained in that domain, require mI≼∇²f≼MI on a convex neighborhood containing that set and every trial segment used in the proof (alternatively impose the bounds globally). With m>0, prove exact-line-search gradient descent objective-gap contraction 1−m/M and the Armijo linear rate with 0<a<1/2, 0<b<1, initial trial step 1 and shrink factor b: accepted t≥min{1,2b(1−a)/M} yields gap contraction at most 1−2am min{1,2b(1−a)/M}. State objective gaps and iterate errors separately. For damped Newton require a Lipschitz Hessian on that convex trial neighborhood and prove finite damped steps followed by accepted unit steps and quadratic convergence. Prove ||x̃−x*||≤η/μ for a μ-strongly convex f when ||∇f(x̃)||≤η; include computed-gradient error δ by replacing η with η+δ. Do not assert global optimization for nonconvex or multimodal likelihoods.

**Proof route:** Use the descent lemma, strong convexity, Armijo decrease and Hessian-Lipschitz Taylor remainder under the stated sublevel invariance. For the gradient residual, use strong monotonicity and Cauchy–Schwarz. Separate optimization residual from an approximate objective/integral and from a model’s statistical target.

**Examples:** strongly convex quadratic with exact rate; damped Newton phase before quadratic convergence; small gradient at a poorly conditioned minimizer.

**Requires:** NA-09; published thm-hessian-characterises-convexity, thm-multivariable-taylor-formula-with-lagrange-remainder, and thm-gradient-and-hessian-of-the-frobenius-least-squares-functional where the least-squares objective is used.

**Sources:** Boyd–Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization §§9.2 and 9.3.1, physical PDF pp. 477–483 / printed pp. 463–469, and §§9.5.1–9.5.3, physical pp. 498–506 / printed pp. 484–492, proofs read: https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/cvxbook/bv_cvxbook.pdf. A: `finite-basis-projector-energies-and-variational-electronic-structure`.

Let S be a supplied Hermitian positive-definite overlap matrix, 0 < r < n, and transform to an orthonormal basis using an existing Cholesky/spectral factorization. Define the compact set P_r = {P=P*, P²=P, tr P=r}. Input finite h=h*, a self-adjoint real-linear map G on Hermitian matrices, and optional real C² functional E_xc on a neighborhood of P_r. Define E(P)=tr(hP)+1/2 tr(PG(P))+E_xc(P) and its Hermitian Frobenius-gradient F(P)=h+G(P)+grad E_xc(P). The conditional finite-basis HF case is E_xc=0 with a supplied symmetry-compatible Coulomb/exchange tensor; the KS-like case is an explicitly supplied density map and differentiable chosen functional. These are mathematical definitions, not assertions of physical exactness. Prove a global minimizer exists, first variation along P(t)=e^{tK}Pe^{-tK} yields [F(P),P]=0, and a sufficient positive tangent-Hessian condition gives an isolated strict local minimizer modulo orbital gauge. A commutator-zero point need not be a minimum and need not occupy the lowest r eigenvalues. Do not silently equate stationarity and Aufbau SCF.

Also include the finite-temperature density domain 0<=D<=I, tr D=r with continuous endpoint convention 0 log 0=0 and entropy term beta^(-1) tr(D log D+(I-D)log(I-D)). Prove compact-domain minimizer existence; on the interior derive the Fermi–Dirac stationarity equation with chemical potential chosen for the trace, and prove uniqueness of that chemical potential for a fixed finite Hermitian F and 0<r<n. This does not prove uniqueness of a self-consistent density for a nonconvex energy. PC-VAR owns spectral trace derivative and endpoint-continuity suppliers; generic constrained KKT/prox comes from optimization owner.

For nested trial spaces, the finite-basis infimum decreases toward the infimum over their union; equality with a continuum infimum additionally requires density in the energy topology and continuity/liminf hypotheses, each proved for the chosen functional. No general Coulomb HF/DFT existence theorem is smuggled into this statement. Source-model error stays separate.

If a specific simple target eigenvalue is separated by certified gap delta from all others, prove sin(angle(u,e))<=rho/delta using spectral expansion; add an upper energy bound from min–max. A residual alone cannot identify the lowest eigenvalue. For a ground state on a compact-resolvent form domain carry the actual form/duality norm and continuum regularity, not the finite-matrix formula verbatim.

pairs.full_design_verbatim:
### UQ2: `global-sensitivity-anova-and-sobol-estimation`

For independent inputs and f∈L²(product law), prove Hoeffding/Sobol decomposition by conditional expectations, orthogonality and variance decomposition; define first/total Sobol indices only for positive output variance. Reuse RQMC b-adic Parseval when it actually matches, but do not identify b-adic frequency blocks with all product-space conditional effects. Derive pick-freeze covariance identities and unbiased numerator estimators (ratio index estimates generally biased); prove consistency and finite-fourth-moment joint CLT/delta-method MCSE under its choice convention. Derive PCE coefficient index formulas from UQ1. For differentiable f under a product law with each one-dimensional Poincaré constant C_i, prove total-effect bound `S_Ti <= C_i E|partial_i f|² / Var f`; establish constants for selected uniform/Gaussian laws or consume exact published supplier. Dependent-input sensitivity needs a different allocation and is explicitly a defined Shapley-effects extension with its own finite permutation algorithm/efficiency identity, not the independent Sobol formula. Sources: Sobol (1993), variance decomposition; Saltelli (2002), estimator identities; Owen (2013), variance components and Sobol indices; Sobol–Kucherenko (2009), derivative-based bounds. B: Ishigami interaction, zero-variance output, correlated-input ambiguity, noisy simulator separating intrinsic noise and input effect. Dependencies UQ1 only for PCE example, existing conditional expectation/Fubini/CLT/delta suppliers; owner supplies general product ANOVA and Poincaré proof.
